title: High-entropy alloy predictive design
bottleneck: High-entropy alloys mix five or more elements in near-equal proportions, creating a compositional space of millions of candidates with potentially exceptional strength, toughness, and corrosion resistance. But phase stability in these complex mixtures is poorly predicted: unwanted brittle intermetallics precipitate unexpectedly, and CALPHAD databases are sparse for multi-principal-element systems. Alloy development remains Edisonian trial and error.
why_it_blocks: These alloys could outperform superalloys in turbines, reactors, and extreme environments, raising efficiency everywhere heat matters. Without predictive design, each alloy costs years of empirical testing, so only a tiny fraction of the space gets explored and adoption stalls.
current_state: Machine learning trained on growing experimental datasets is beginning to predict single-phase stability, and the SuperC consortium's ML-plus-physics pipeline shows how such searches can work. But validated, deployable high-entropy alloys in safety-critical service are still rare.
